memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said, "Put your hand inside your cloak." So Moses put his hand into his cloak, and when he took it out, the skin was leprous—it had become as white as snow. "Now put it back into your cloak," he said. So Moses put his hand back into his cloak, and when he took it out, it was restored, like the rest of his flesh." - Exodus 4:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This second sign is harder than the first. Moses is not asked to hold a snake; he is asked to watch his own body become diseased.

Leprosy in Israel meant exclusion — from worship, from community, from touch. To see it appear on his own hand would have been terrifying. And then, just as quickly, God restores it completely.

The message is clear: the God who allows affliction is the God who heals. Both the wounding and the restoring were in His hand.

That is a hard truth, and Scripture does not soften it. God is sovereign over suffering as well as over healing. We may not understand why He permits what He permits. But we are never dealing with two competing powers — only one Lord, who is good.

Centuries later, a leper came to Jesus and said, if You are willing, You can make me clean. Jesus did what no one else would do: He touched him (Mk 1:41). The God of the healed hand took on hands of His own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust God's goodness even when He permits what I would not choose?
2. What do I need to bring to Jesus with the words "if You are willing"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are sovereign over both my suffering and my healing. I trust Your goodness even where I cannot trace Your reasons. Amen.
